questions.q: In the standard anatomical position, how do the palms of the hands face?
questions.explain: In the standard anatomical position, the body stands upright facing forward with the upper limbs at the sides and the palms facing anteriorly. Facing posteriorly occurs during pronation.

open.q: In the standard anatomical position, what direction do the palms of the hands face?

questions.q: In the standard anatomical position, which direction do the toes point?
questions.explain: In the standard anatomical position, the feet are slightly apart with the toes pointing anteriorly. Lateral or medial rotation of the lower limb shifts the direction the toes point.

open.q: In the standard anatomical position, what direction do the toes point?

questions.q: Which vertical plane passes longitudinally through the midline of the body to divide it into equal right and left halves?
questions.explain: The median (midsagittal) plane passes through the center of the body to create equal left and right halves. Parasagittal planes are parallel to the median plane but off-center.

open.q: Which vertical plane passes longitudinally through the midline of the body to divide it into equal right and left halves?

questions.q: Which plane divides the body or an organ into anterior and posterior portions?
questions.explain: The coronal (frontal) plane is a vertical plane oriented at right angles to the median plane that separates anterior from posterior parts. Transverse planes divide superior from inferior parts.

open.q: Which anatomical plane divides the body or an organ into anterior and posterior portions?

questions.q: A vertical plane passes parallel to the median plane, dividing the right half of the chest into unequal medial and lateral parts. What is this plane called?
questions.explain: Any vertical plane parallel to the median plane that is not on the midline is a parasagittal plane. Coronal planes run side-to-side, and axial planes are horizontal.

open.q: What is a vertical plane that lies parallel to the median plane and divides the body into unequal right and left parts?

questions.q: Which directional term describes a position closer to the point of attachment of a limb to the trunk?
questions.explain: Proximal indicates greater proximity to the trunk or point of origin of a limb, whereas distal indicates greater distance from that attachment point.

open.q: Which directional term refers to a location closer to the trunk or point of attachment of a limb?

questions.q: Which directional term means closer to the median plane of the body?
questions.explain: Medial means nearer to the median plane, while lateral means farther away from the median plane. External and internal describe positions relative to the center of an organ or cavity.

open.q: Which directional term means closer to the median plane of the body?

questions.q: Which pair of terms is most commonly used to describe positions on the dorsum or palm of the hand?
questions.explain: Dorsal refers to the back of the hand and palmar refers to the palm of the hand, avoiding confusion with anterior and posterior when limb positions change. On the foot, the equivalent terms are dorsal and plantar.

open.q: Which two directional terms describe the back surface and palm surface of the hand?

questions.q: When describing structures on the sole of the foot regardless of foot position, which term is preferred over inferior?
questions.explain: Plantar specifically denotes the sole of the foot, whereas dorsal denotes the top (dorsum) of the foot. Rostral and cranial refer to headward directions.

open.q: Which directional term specifically describes the sole of the foot?

questions.q: Which term describes two structures that occur on the same side of the body?
questions.explain: Ipsilateral refers to structures on the same side of the body, such as the right thumb and right great toe. Contralateral refers to opposite sides of the body.

open.q: Which term describes structures located on the same side of the body?

questions.q: A patient has a stroke affecting the left motor cortex and develops weakness in the right arm. How is the right arm weakness described relative to the left brain lesion?
questions.explain: Contralateral means occurring on the opposite side of the body relative to another structure or lesion. Because most corticospinal fibers decussate in the medulla, a left cerebral lesion causes right-sided motor deficits.

open.q: A patient has a left cerebral hemisphere lesion causing weakness in the right upper limb. What term describes the relationship of the right limb weakness to the left brain lesion?

questions.q: Which term means situated closer to the head or upper end of the body?
questions.explain: Superior (or cranial) means nearer to the vertex or head end of the body. Inferior (or caudal) means nearer to the feet or tail end.

open.q: Which directional term means closer to the head or upper end of the body?

questions.q: Which directional term indicates a position closer to the surface of the body?
questions.explain: Superficial describes structures closer to the body surface, whereas deep (or profundus) describes structures farther from the surface.

open.q: Which directional term indicates a position closer to the surface of the body?

questions.q: Which movement bends a joint or decreases the angle between two bones in the sagittal plane?
questions.explain: Flexion generally decreases the angle between articulating bones and usually occurs in a sagittal plane. Extension straightens a joint and typically increases the angle between bones.

open.q: Which joint movement typically decreases the angle between articulating bones in a sagittal plane?

questions.q: Moving the arm away from the trunk in the coronal plane is called which movement?
questions.explain: Abduction moves a limb or digit away from the median plane or axial reference line in the coronal plane. Adduction moves it toward the median plane or midline of the hand/foot.

open.q: What is the movement of a limb away from the median plane of the body in the coronal plane?

questions.q: Which movement rotates the radius over the ulna so the palm of the hand faces posteriorly when starting from the anatomical position?
questions.explain: Pronation rotates the forearm and hand so the palm faces posteriorly (or inferiorly when the elbow is flexed). Supination turns the palm anteriorly or superiorly.

open.q: Which movement of the forearm rotates the radius across the ulna so the palm faces posteriorly from the anatomical position?

questions.q: Turning the sole of the foot away from the median plane (laterally) is known as which movement?
questions.explain: Eversion turns the plantar surface of the foot laterally away from the median plane, while inversion turns the sole medially toward the median plane.

open.q: What movement turns the sole of the foot laterally away from the median plane?

questions.q: A pianist brings the thumb across the palm to touch the tip of the little finger. Which specialized thumb movement is this?
questions.explain: Opposition brings the pad of the thumb into contact with the pad of another digit through combined flexion and medial rotation at the carpometacarpal joint. Reposition returns the thumb to its anatomical position.

open.q: What movement brings the pad of the thumb across the palm to touch another digit?

questions.q: Which movement of the foot raises the anterior part of the foot and toes toward the leg?
questions.explain: Dorsiflexion flexes the ankle joint so the dorsum of the foot moves superiorly toward the anterior leg. Plantarflexion depresses the toes and points the foot inferiorly.

open.q: Which ankle movement lifts the front of the foot and toes superiorly toward the leg?

questions.q: Which circular sequence combines flexion, abduction, extension, and adduction of a limb?
questions.explain: Circumduction is a sequential circular movement combining flexion, abduction, extension, and adduction so the distal end of the limb traces a circle. Rotation turns a limb or body part around its longitudinal axis.

open.q: Which movement combines flexion, abduction, extension, and adduction in sequence so a limb describes a cone?
